doc.md:
Represents a widget tooltip.

Basic tooltips can be realized simply by using
[`Widget.set_tooltip_text()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_tooltip_text) or
[`Widget.set_tooltip_markup()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_tooltip_markup) without
any explicit tooltip object.

When you need a tooltip with a little more fancy contents,
like adding an image, or you want the tooltip to have different
contents per `GtkTreeView` row or cell, you will have to do a
little more work:

- Set the [`Widget:has-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:has-tooltip) property to `TRUE`.
  This will make GTK monitor the widget for motion and related events
  which are needed to determine when and where to show a tooltip.

- Connect to the [`Widget::query-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:query-tooltip) signal.
  This signal will be emitted when a tooltip is supposed to be shown.
  One of the arguments passed to the signal handler is a `GtkTooltip`
  object. This is the object that we are about to display as a tooltip,
  and can be manipulated in your callback using functions like
  [`Tooltip.set_icon()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Tooltip#method:set_icon). There are functions for setting
  the tooltip’s markup, setting an image from a named icon, or even
  putting in a custom widget.

- Return `TRUE` from your ::query-tooltip handler. This causes the tooltip
  to be show. If you return `FALSE`, it will not be shown.

set_custom.brief: Replaces the widget packed into the tooltip with `custom_widget`.
set_custom.md:
Replaces the widget packed into the tooltip with
`custom_widget`. `custom_widget` does not get destroyed when the tooltip goes
away.
By default a box with a `GtkImage` and `GtkLabel` is embedded in
the tooltip, which can be configured using gtk_tooltip_set_markup()
and gtk_tooltip_set_icon().

set_icon.brief: Sets the icon of the tooltip (which is in front of the text) to be `paintable`.
set_icon.md:
Sets the icon of the tooltip (which is in front of the text) to be
`paintable`.  If `paintable` is `NULL`, the image will be hidden.

set_icon_from_gicon.brief: Sets the icon of the tooltip (which is in front of the text) to be the icon indicated by `gicon` with the size indicated by `size`.
set_icon_from_gicon.md:
Sets the icon of the tooltip (which is in front of the text)
to be the icon indicated by `gicon` with the size indicated
by `size`. If `gicon` is `NULL`, the image will be hidden.

set_icon_from_icon_name.brief: Sets the icon of the tooltip (which is in front of the text) to be the icon indicated by `icon_name` with the size indicated by `size`.
set_icon_from_icon_name.md:
Sets the icon of the tooltip (which is in front of the text) to be
the icon indicated by `icon_name` with the size indicated
by `size`.  If `icon_name` is `NULL`, the image will be hidden.

set_markup.brief: Sets the text of the tooltip to be `markup`.
set_markup.md:
Sets the text of the tooltip to be `markup`.

The string must be marked up with Pango markup.
If `markup` is `NULL`, the label will be hidden.

set_text.brief: Sets the text of the tooltip to be `text`.
set_text.md:
Sets the text of the tooltip to be `text`.

If `text` is `NULL`, the label will be hidden.
See also [`Tooltip.set_markup()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Tooltip#method:set_markup).

set_tip_area.brief: Sets the area of the widget, where the contents of this tooltip apply, to be `rect` (in widget coordinates).
set_tip_area.md:
Sets the area of the widget, where the contents of this tooltip apply,
to be `rect` (in widget coordinates).  This is especially useful for
properly setting tooltips on `GtkTreeView` rows and cells, `GtkIconViews`,
etc.

For setting tooltips on `GtkTreeView`, please refer to the convenience
functions for this: gtk_tree_view_set_tooltip_row() and
gtk_tree_view_set_tooltip_cell().
